newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Rafinerska H1 gross profit up 38 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech Rafinerska H1 gross profit up 38 pct.

text.p: First half gross profit at the main Czech crude oil refinery, Ceska Rafinerska a.s., rose to 580 million crowns from 420 million crowns in the first six months of last year, the company said in a statement.

Rafinerska -- 49 percent owned by a western consortium comprised of Du Pont de Nemours Co. unit Conoco, Italy's Agip SpA, and Royal Dutch/Shell -- said its turnover for the period rose 40 million crowns to 16.299 billion crowns.
Further financial results were not disclosed.

The statement quoted financial director Barry Kumins as saying that the result met the company's goals despite the increase in costs connected with the planned halt in production at the Litvinov refinery "and despite the unfavourable fall in the Czech currency exchange rate".
The Czech crown has lost nearly 33 percent against the dollar since its peak against the U.S. currency last autumn and more than 13 percent from its peak against the German mark in February.

Rafinerska, which was created in 1995 when the state sold a minority stake in the combined refinery assets of the Litvinov and Kaucuk petrochemical plants to the consortium, imports its crude oil for production mostly from Russia.
